back: Every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen (lottery, random numbers).
Choosing at regular intervals, such as every 10th house or every 5th person.
Dividing the population into groups and sampling each group in proportion to its size.
notes: E.g. 5% of each Form in a school.

back: A small trial of a questionnaire or method to find and fix problems before the main survey.
Closed: fixed answers, easy to count and graph. Open: own words, richer but harder to analyse.
Straight lines joining people's origins to a destination; together they show its sphere of influence.
Scoring a place on criteria between two opposite descriptions (e.g. −2 very noisy to +2 very quiet) and totalling the scores.
notes: Subjective: keep the same scorers or use means.

back: Same length of count, same times of day, a tally sheet and an agreed counting rule at every site.
